name: Cape Canaveral Launch Complex 36B (LC-36B)
best_known_for: USAF Atlas-Centaur pad — launched Mariner 10 (first Mercury flyby, 1973), Pioneer 11 (first Saturn flyby, 1973), and most early Surveyor + Pioneer Venus missions
credit: Cape Canaveral Launch Complex 36B was the second of two Atlas-Centaur pads at Cape Canaveral (alongside LC-36A, built first). LC-36B first flew 1965-08-11 with Atlas-Centaur AC-6, a suborbital qualification flight, and became the workhorse pad for the high-energy Atlas-Centaur stack — flying Mariner 10 (1973-11-03, first Mercury flyby), Pioneer 11 (1973-04-06, first Saturn flyby), Pioneer Venus 1 + 2 (1978), and the Intelsat / Inmarsat / Hot Bird commercial GEO comsats through the 1990s and early 2000s. Final flight 2005-02-03 — Atlas IIIB AC-208 launching MILSTAR DFS-3 — the last Atlas IIIB launch and last LC-36B flight under USAF auspices. The complex was leased to Blue Origin in 2015 and demolished + rebuilt as the Blue Origin New Glenn pad (LC-36 unified), with first New Glenn flight 2025-01-16. The original LC-36B mobile service tower was felled 2007-06-16.
